topic: Constellations at Different Times of the Year
key_concepts: Stars differ in brightness, size, and color
A star's color indicates its approximate surface temperature
Apparent magnitude is brightness seen from Earth; absolute magnitude is brightness at 10 p
Constellations are recognizable star patterns and IAU-defined sky boundaries
Asterisms are recognizable star patterns within constellations, such as the Big Dipper in
There are 88 modern constellations, many based on Greek groupings
Ursa Major and Ursa Minor are spoon-shaped constellations of seven bright stars
Earth's rotation makes stars appear to move from east to west
Polaris lies near the north celestial pole and is called the North Star
Circumpolar stars near celestial poles remain visible all year
Northern circumpolar constellations include Ursa Major, Ursa Minor, Cassiopeia, and Draco
Constellation visibility depends on observer location and time of year
